# Caboodle: Feature Context

A map of every module, feature and sub-feature in the Caboodle product, built from the code of its three repositories. It is meant for developers and AI agents who need to understand or change part of the product safely.

**How to read this file**

- **Paths** start with the repository folder name and are relative to the folder that holds all three repositories: `caboodle.web/...`, `caboodle.admin/...`, `caboodle.backend/...`. Backend module code lives under `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/Modules/<Module>/Modules.<Module>.Application|Domain`.
- **Endpoints** are written as `METHOD /api/v1/<controller>/<route>`. The prefix comes from `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/Hosts/API/Controllers/VersionedApiController.cs`; four controllers override it (noted in their sections).
- **Numbering** is fixed: `2.N` is a module, `2.N.M` a feature, `2.N.M.K` a sub-feature. Every feature uses the same field order, so sections can be scanned or parsed.
- **Status** values: Active (reachable and working), Partial (built but incomplete), Deprecated (still in code but superseded or unreachable), Feature-flagged (gated by a code constant or configuration value).
- **Secrets**: configuration and environment values are never reproduced; only key and variable names appear.

Each affected module records the difference under "Gotchas / tech debt". |

## 0. Product Overview

### 0.1 Purpose

Caboodle is a multi-tenant SaaS for natural and organic consumer packaged goods (CPG) brands and the brokerages that sell for them. It replaces spreadsheet workflows with one system for:

- planning, approving and tracking trade promotions (2.6, 2.7);
- broker category review and brand reporting workflows (2.8, 2.9);
- ingesting distributor and syndicated data such as KeHE, UNFI, SPINS and distributor sales reports (2.10, 2.14);
- sales and promotion analytics, including an AI assistant (2.11, 2.12);
- shared CRM and product master data (2.4, 2.5) and a file repository (2.13).

### 0.2 Users and roles

| User type | How the system identifies them | Where defined |
|---|---|---|
| Platform admin | Identity role `ADMIN`; endpoints use `[MustHavePermission]`; signs in to `caboodle.admin` through `POST /api/v1/admin/login`. A platform admin with no company is sent to `/use-admin-app` by the web app. | `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Core/Shared/Authorization/CaboodleRoles.cs`, `CaboodlePermissions.cs`; `caboodle.web/src/components/AccessRedirectGuard.tsx` |
| Brand company member | Organization of type Brand (5); system org roles `brand-admin` and `brand-member`. A Brand company has exactly one brand: itself. | `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Core/Shared/Authorization/OrgRoles.cs` |
| Brokerage member | Organization of type Brokerage (10); system org roles `brokerage-admin` and `broker`. Works on brands through brand connections, with per-brand module access and separate "company access" for the brokerage's own data. | same file; see 2.2 |
| Signed in, no company | Sent to `/onboarding` to request access or create a company | `caboodle.web/src/components/AccessRedirectGuard.tsx` |
| Legacy roles | Identity roles `UNASSIGNED`, `BRANDOWNER`, `BROKER`, `BRANDSUBUSER`, `BROKERSUBUSER`. Still seeded and still read by `BrandValidationMiddleware` and not-yet-migrated endpoints; new code must not use them. | `CaboodleRoles.cs`; `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure/Middleware/BrandValidationMiddleware.cs` |

Organization permissions (`OrgPermissions`): `organization.view`, `organization.update`, `member.view|invite|approve|update|suspend|remove`, `domain.view|manage`, `connection.view`, `access.manage`, `files.private` (`caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Core/Shared/Authorization/OrgPermissions.cs`). Module access is per person and per brand, by module slug and action (View, Create, Update, Delete, Import, Export). The full model is in 2.2.

### 0.3 High-level architecture

```
 Browser                Browser
    |                      |
 caboodle.web           caboodle.admin
 Next.js 14 :3000       Next.js 16 :3004
 (NextAuth, /api/ai-message placeholder)
    |  Authorization, OrganizationID, BrandID headers
    v                      v
 caboodle.backend  ASP.NET Core (.NET 6) :5060  /api/v1/*
    |-- PostgreSQL (EF Core writes, Dapper reads, Hangfire storage)
    |-- AWS S3 (files, exports, imports)      |-- SMTP mail + SNS delivery webhook
    |-- LLM providers (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini) |-- Google Geocoding
    |-- web crawler service (data sync)        |-- external SQL Server "Bubbies" (admin probe)
```

| Unit | Entry point | Talks to |
|---|---|---|
| Customer web app | `caboodle.web/src/app/layout.tsx`; started with `next start -p 3000` | Backend at `NEXT_PUBLIC_CABOODLE_API_URL` + `/api/v1` (`caboodle.web/src/constants/appConstants.ts`); own routes `/api/auth/[...nextauth]` and `/api/ai-message` |
| Platform admin app | `caboodle.admin/src/app/layout.tsx`; `next start -p 3004` | Backend at `NEXT_PUBLIC_CABOODLE_API_URL` with version `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_VERSION` (`caboodle.admin/src/appConstant/constant.ts`); own route `/api/auth/[...nextauth]` |
| Backend API | `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/Hosts/API/Program.cs`, module wiring in `ModuleStartup.cs` | PostgreSQL, Hangfire, S3, SMTP, SNS (inbound), Seq logging, Google Geocoding, LLM providers, a web crawler at a hard-coded internal URL (`caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/Modules/Shared/Modules.Shared.Infrastructure/Services/DataSync/DataSyncJobService.cs`), the external "Bubbies" SQL Server |

- Neither front end proxies API calls (`caboodle.web/next.config.js`, `caboodle.admin/next.config.js` have no rewrites), so the browser calls the API origin directly and backend CORS applies.
- The backend reads the `OrganizationID` and `BrandID` headers in `CurrentUserMiddleware` (`caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure/Auth/CurrentUserMiddleware.cs`); the web app sets them in `caboodle.web/src/components/AxiosInterceptor.tsx`.
- A SignalR hub is mapped at `/notifications` (`caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure/Notifications/Startup.cs`), but no front end connects to it.
- Two EF contexts share one PostgreSQL connection: `ApplicationDbContext` (ASP.NET Identity, audit trails) and `MainDbContext` (all module tables, about 121 `DbSet`s) (`caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/Modules/Shared/Modules.Shared.Infrastructure/Persistence/MainDbContext.cs`). Tables are split by schema: `CRM`, `ProductSpecs`, `DataUpload`, `Brand`, `TradeSpend`, `TradeSpendSandbox`, `FileRepository`, `Email`, `Broker`, `DataHub`, `Intelligence`, `Configuration`, `DataLifecycle`, `Organization`, `Identity`, `Auditing`.
- Hosting: Docker images pushed to AWS ECR and started with `docker run` on hosts reached over SSH (`caboodle.backend/bitbucket-pipelines.yml`, `caboodle.admin/bitbucket-pipelines.yml`). The web app's deploy steps are commented out in `caboodle.web/bitbucket-pipelines.yml`. Details in 3.13.

### 0.4 Tech stack (versions from the manifests)

The stack line in the documentation request does not match the code: the web app runs Next.js 14.2.35 on React 18.3.1 and the admin app runs Next.js 16.2.11 on React 18.2.0. No repository uses Next.js 13.4 or React 19.

| Layer | caboodle.web | caboodle.admin | caboodle.backend |
|---|---|---|---|
| Framework | Next.js 14.2.35 (App Router), React 18.3.1, TypeScript 5.1.6 | Next.js 16.2.11 (App Router), React 18.2.0, TypeScript 5.1.6 | ASP.NET Core on .NET 6 (`global.json`, every `.csproj` targets `net6.0`) |
| UI | antd 5.23.2, PrimeReact 10.9.2, Tailwind 3.3.3, AG Grid 31, ECharts 5, Mapbox GL 3, FortuneSheet, CKEditor 5 | antd 5.29.3, Tailwind, ECharts 6 | n/a |
| Data and state | React Query 4.33, Zustand 4.4, axios 1.4 | React Query 4.44, axios 1.18 | EF Core 6.0.2 + Npgsql 6.0.3, Dapper 2.0.123, EFCore.BulkExtensions 6.5, MediatR 10, FluentValidation 10, Mapster 7, Ardalis.Specification 6 |
| Auth | next-auth 4.23 (credentials, JWT) | next-auth 4.24 | JWT bearer (Azure AD option present, off) |
| Jobs and logs | n/a | n/a | Hangfire 1.7.28 on PostgreSQL, Serilog 5 (Seq, file, console), NSwag 13 |
| Tests | Jest 29 + Testing Library | Jest (see 3.12) | xUnit + Moq + coverlet |

Sources: `caboodle.web/package.json`, `caboodle.admin/package.json`, `caboodle.backend/Directory.Build.props`, the module `.csproj` files.

### 0.5 Modules and how they relate

| # | Module | Owns |
|---|---|---|
| 2.1 | Identity & Authentication | Accounts, login, tokens, sign-up and verification, password reset, profile, legacy roles and sub-users, admin user management |
| 2.2 | Organizations & Access Control | Organizations, memberships, org roles, invitations, access requests, domains, brand connections, per-brand module access, module catalog and settings, audit events, onboarding, Company area |
| 2.3 | Brands & Brokers | Brand and broker records and the legacy brand-to-broker links |
| 2.4 | CRM | Retailers, banners, banner SKUs, distributors, distribution centers, regions, contacts, stores, pipeline |
| 2.5 | Product Specifications | Categories, products, price lists |
| 2.6 | Trade Promotion Planning | Sandbox promotions and versions, Brand Approved promotions, Simple Promotion grid, events, fees, the calculation engine |
| 2.7 | Promotional Calendars & Management | Brand Promotional Calendar, broker Promotional Management, promotional notes, custom Promo Tabs |
| 2.8 | Category Review & Brand Report | Broker category reviews, review calendar, brand reports, notifications and email logs |
| 2.9 | Market Overview & APL Reports | Market overview logs and reports, Distributor APL, Retail APL, Brand APL and activities, broker landing page |
| 2.10 | Data Uploads | KeHE, UNFI, SPINS, distributor sales reports, master data bulk import and export, data mappings, chunked imports |
| 2.11 | Reports & Dashboards | Trade spend roll-up, monthly report, sales tracker, product report, brand dashboard |
| 2.12 | Intelligence (Ask Caboodle) | AI chat over Caboodle data |
| 2.13 | File Repository | Brand file explorer, broker file repository, share links |
| 2.14 | DataHub | Admin data quality: entity resolution, store list, matching, mapped and unmapped records, data sync |
| 2.15 | Platform Administration | Soft delete purge, email logs and SNS webhook, file key backfill, data cleanup tools, admin dashboard |

Main dependency flow (detail in section 4):

```
2.1 Identity  <-->  2.2 Organizations & Access  <-- every module (authorization, module settings)
2.4 CRM + 2.5 Product Specs  -->  master data read by 2.6 to 2.12
2.10 Data Uploads  -->  2.14 DataHub (mapping, store list)  -->  2.9, 2.11, 2.12 read resolved data
2.6 Trade Promotion Planning  -->  2.7 Calendars, 2.11 Reports, 2.12 Intelligence
2.8 Category Review  -->  2.3 Brands (people picker), email via 2.15 logging
2.15 Platform Administration  -->  maintenance writes into 2.4, 2.5, 2.6, 2.13
```

## 1. Inventory Tree

One line per node: number, name, status, description. Every entry point found in discovery maps to a node here; the full mapping is in each module's code map and APIs table. Host-level entry points with no business feature are listed under "Platform and host" at the end of this tree and described in section 3.

- **2.1 Module: Identity & Authentication** [Active]: accounts, credentials, JWT and refresh tokens, sign-up with email code, password reset, own profile, legacy roles and platform permissions, legacy sub-users, admin user management, NextAuth plumbing in web and admin
  - **2.1.1 Feature: Login and session lifecycle** [Active]: `POST auth/login` issues a 24 h JWT and a 14-day refresh token; web NextAuth credentials session; text-based failure branching
    - **2.1.1.1 Sub-feature: Token refresh and rotation** [Active]: `auth/refresh-token` rotates the refresh token, 60 s grace for the previous one, web refreshes 10 min before expiry
    - **2.1.1.2 Sub-feature: Logout and refresh-token revocation** [Active]: `auth/logout` clears refresh tokens and audits; web clears per-person storage
    - **2.1.1.3 Sub-feature: Web token holder and 401 handling** [Active]: module-level token for axios, one refresh and one retry on 401, sign-out on refresh error
    - **2.1.1.4 Sub-feature: Master password sign-in** [Feature-flagged]: `SecuritySettings:MasterPassword` signs in to any account; set in all three environment appsettings
    - **2.1.1.5 Sub-feature: Azure AD bearer authentication** [Feature-flagged]: inactive because `SecuritySettings:Provider` is `Jwt` everywhere
  - **2.1.2 Feature: Sign-up and email verification** [Active]: `POST registration` creates an inactive UNASSIGNED account, emails a 6-digit code, verify activates it
    - **2.1.2.1 Sub-feature: 6-digit code verification** [Active]: HMAC-stored codes, 10 min, 5 tries, 30 s resend cooldown, enumeration-safe answers

## 2. Module Sections

### 2.1 Module: Identity & Authentication

- **Purpose:** Owns the person's account (ASP.NET Core Identity user), credentials, sign-in tokens, sign-up with email verification, password reset, the user's own profile, the legacy user-wide roles and platform permissions, legacy sub-user and legacy invitation flows, platform-admin account management, and the sign-in plumbing of both Next.js apps (NextAuth credentials provider, refresh, logout, 401 handling). Company membership, roles inside a company, module access and `/me/access` are not owned here (see Cross-module dependencies).
- **Key paths:**
  - Backend controllers: `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/Hosts/API/Controllers/Identity/AuthController.cs`, `Identity/UsersController.cs`, `Identity/RolesController.cs`, `Profile/ProfileController.cs`, `Registration/RegistrationController.cs`, `Modules/SubUsers/SubUsersController.cs`, plus `Admin/AdminController.cs#LoginAsync` only.

#### 2.1.1 Feature: Login and session lifecycle

- **Status:** Active
- **What it does:** Exchanges email and password for a signed HS256 JWT access token plus an opaque refresh token, rotates the refresh token on refresh, and revokes it on logout. The customer web app wraps this in a NextAuth credentials provider whose JWT cookie holds both tokens; a module-level token holder feeds axios, and a 401 triggers one refresh and one retry before sign-out. Used by every person with an account (no role or module gate; `[AllowAnonymous]` for login and refresh, `[Authorize]` for logout).
- **User flow:**
  1. Person opens the web root `/`; `caboodle.web/src/app/page.tsx` calls `getServerSession` and redirects to `/dashboard` or `/login`.
  2. `/login` (`caboodle.web/src/components/Auth/LoginForm.tsx`) calls NextAuth `signIn("credentials", { email, password, tenantId: "root", redirect: false })`.
  3. NextAuth `authorize` (`caboodle.web/src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/options.ts`) calls `CaboodleService.login` → `POST /api/v1/auth/login`.
  4. Backend `TokenService.SignInAsync`: unknown email or wrong password → 400 `Auth` "Incorrect username or password."; correct password but unverified email → 400 `Email` "Email not confirmed."; inactive → 400 `Auth` "User not active.". The password is checked first so a wrong password reveals nothing else.
  5. On success the backend rotates the refresh token, returns `AuthDto { tokenInfo, userInfo }`, and audits `auth.login_succeeded` (portal `app`); a failure audits `auth.login_failed` with the reason.
  6. The NextAuth `jwt` callback stores `accessToken`, `accessTokenExpiry`, `refreshToken`, `refreshTokenExpiryTime`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `imageUrl`; the `session` callback exposes `accessToken`, `accessTokenExpiry`, `error`.
  7. The form branches on the exact error text (`caboodle.web/src/helper/login.helper.ts` `resolveLoginFailure`): "Email not confirmed." resends a code and routes to `/verify-email?email=`; "User not active." shows an in-place warning; anything else is a toast. On success it clears the persisted brand store and routes to `/dashboard`, or to `/invitations/{token}` when `?invite=` is a GUID.
  8. `?verified=1` shows "Email verified" and `?email=` prefills the form.
  9. Every later session read within 10 minutes of access-token expiry refreshes the token (see 2.1.1.1). Logout: see 2.1.1.2.
- **Code map:**

| Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/Hosts/API/Controllers/Identity/AuthController.cs` | `login`, `refresh-token`, `logout`; client IP from `X-Forwarded-For` or the connection |
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure/Identity/TokenService.cs` | Sign-in checks, JWT creation, refresh rotation and grace window, logout, audit |
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure/Auth/Startup.cs` | Registers current user, permissions, Identity, `SecuritySettings`, OTP; picks Azure AD or JWT bearer from `SecuritySettings:Provider` |
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure/Auth/Jwt/Startup.cs` | JWT bearer validation (symmetric key, lifetime, zero clock skew, no issuer or audience check), 401 and 403 envelopes, `access_token` query for `/notifications` |
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure/Auth/CurrentUserMiddleware.cs` | Sets `ICurrentUser` from claims plus `BrandID` and `OrganizationID` headers |
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure/Startup.cs` | Pipeline order `UseAuthentication → UseCurrentUser → UseAuthorization → UseBrandValidationMiddleware`; `MapControllers().RequireAuthorization()` makes every endpoint authenticated unless `[AllowAnonymous]` |
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure/Identity/Startup.cs` | Identity options: password min length 6, no complexity rules, unique email |
| `caboodle.web/src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/options.ts` | Credentials provider, `jwt` and `session` callbacks, `refreshAccessToken`, `describeLoginError`, `secret: NEXTAUTH_SECRET`, `maxAge` 14 days |
| `caboodle.web/src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts` | NextAuth GET/POST handler |
| `caboodle.web/src/app/page.tsx` | Server redirect root to `/dashboard` or `/login` |
| `caboodle.web/src/app/(auth)/layout.tsx` | Auth shell; a signed-in visitor goes to `/dashboard`, to `/invitations/{code}` for an invitation link, or is logged out for any other `?code=` link |
| `caboodle.web/src/app/(auth)/login/page.tsx`, `caboodle.web/src/components/Auth/LoginForm.tsx` | Login page and form |
| `caboodle.web/src/helper/login.helper.ts` | `parseLoginError`, `resolveLoginFailure`, `resolvePostLoginRoute` |
| `caboodle.web/src/service/caboodle.service.ts` | `CaboodleService.login`, `CaboodleService.refreshAccessToken` |
| `caboodle.web/src/helper/serverSession.helper.ts` | `serverSessionCheck` used by `(brand)`, `(broker)`, `(company)` layouts; redirect `/` when no session |
| `caboodle.web/src/components/AuthProvider.tsx` | `SessionProvider` + `SessionTokenSync` in the root layout |
| `caboodle.web/nextauth.d.ts` | `Session.accessToken`, `accessTokenExpiry`, `error` typing |
| `caboodle.web/src/models/genericModel.ts` | `LoginModel`, `TokenModel`, `RefreshTokenPostModel` |

- **Data:** `Identity.Users` token columns (`RefreshToken`, `RefreshTokenExpiryTime`, `PreviousRefreshToken`, `RefreshTokenRotatedOn`); IAM audit events table (owned by 2.2). JWT claims (`TokenService.GetClaims`): `nameidentifier` (user id), `email`, `fullName`, `name`, `surname`, `ipAddress`, `image_url`, `mobilephone`. No role and no permission claims are in the token.
- **APIs/interfaces:**

| Method | Path | Access rule | Request / Response | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | /api/v1/auth/login | `AllowAnonymous` | `TokenRequest(Email, Password)` / `AuthDto { TokenInfo: TokenResponse(Token, TokenExpiryTime, RefreshToken, RefreshTokenExpiryTime), UserInfo: UserDetailsDto }` | `AuthController.LoginAsync` → `TokenService.GetTokenAsync` |
| POST | /api/v1/auth/refresh-token | `AllowAnonymous` | `RefreshTokenRequest(Token, RefreshToken)` / `AuthDto` | `AuthController.RefreshTokenAsync` → `TokenService.RefreshTokenAsync` |
| POST | /api/v1/auth/logout | `Authorize` | none / 204 | `AuthController.LogoutAsync` → `TokenService.LogoutAsync` |
| GET, POST | /api/auth/[...nextauth] (web Next.js route) | NextAuth | NextAuth session and credentials callback | `caboodle.web/src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts` |

  Audit events: `auth.login_succeeded`, `auth.login_failed` (metadata `portal`, `reason`), `auth.logout`.
- **Business rules:**
  - Failure order (`TokenService.GetSignInFailureAsync`): unknown user, wrong password, email not confirmed (only when `SecuritySettings:RequireConfirmedAccount`, `true` in all environments), inactive, not admin (admin portal only).
  - Unknown user and wrong password return the same text, so login cannot enumerate accounts.
  - Access token lifetime `SecuritySettings:JwtSettings:TokenExpirationInMinutes` = 1440 (24 h) and refresh token `RefreshTokenExpirationInDays` = 14 in Development, Staging and Production appsettings.
  - Refresh token is 32 random bytes, Base64 (`TokenService.GenerateRefreshToken`).
  - Web NextAuth session `maxAge` is 14 days to match the refresh token (`SESSION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS`).
  - Web `redirect` callback always returns `NEXT_PUBLIC_NEXTAUTH_URL` when set, ignoring the requested URL.
- **Dependencies:** ASP.NET Core Identity (`UserManager`), `System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt`, Mapster; next-auth v4 credentials provider; env `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_NEXTAUTH_URL`; backend config `SecuritySettings` (`Provider`, `RequireConfirmedAccount`, `JwtSettings:Key`, `MasterPassword`); IAM audit (2.2).
- **Errors & edge cases:**
  - All login failures are 400 except admin-portal "not admin" (401). The web `authorize` serialises `{ key, message }` into the NextAuth error string; the admin one forwards the whole `messages` object.
  - `Email` key carries both "Invalid Email Address." (validator) and "Email not confirmed."; `Auth` carries both "Incorrect username or password." and "User not active.", so both frontends branch on the exact text.
  - `USE_MOCK_DATA` (`caboodle.web/src/constants/appConstants.ts`, currently `false`) makes `authorize` and refresh return `mockAuthUser`.
- **Tests:** backend `caboodle.backend/caboodle/tests/Infrastructure.Test/Identity/TokenServiceTests.cs` (15 cases: failure order, admin role check, rotation, grace window, inactive and unconfirmed refresh, malformed and tampered token, audit, logout); web `caboodle.web/src/__tests__/app/auth/nextAuthOptions.test.ts` (13), `caboodle.web/src/__tests__/components/Auth/LoginForm.test.tsx` (7), `caboodle.web/src/__tests__/helper/login.helper.test.ts` (4). Gap: no API-level test of the login endpoint; `serverSessionCheck` untested.
- **Gotchas / tech debt:**
  - **Master password (security):** `TokenService.GetSignInFailureAsync` accepts `SecuritySettings:MasterPassword` as the password for any account. The key is set in `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/Hosts/API/appsettings.Development.json`, `appsettings.Staging.json` and `appsettings.Production.json` (values not reproduced here). See 2.1.1.4.
  - JWT validation does not check issuer or audience (`Jwt/Startup.cs`); the same symmetric key signs every token.
  - Web `serverSessionCheck` does not reject a session carrying `error: "RefreshAccessTokenError"` (the admin layout does); the client `SessionTokenSync` signs out instead.
  - Web `signIn` sends `tenantId: "root"`, which `authorize` never forwards; `LoginModel.tenantId` is vestigial.
  - `caboodle.web/src/components/Auth/Login.tsx` is imported nowhere (old single-page auth switcher); `caboodle.web/src/hooks/auth.ts` is an empty file; `caboodle.web/src/app/page.tsx` imports the login page but only redirects.
  - Five of six web env files lack `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` (only `caboodle.web/.env.dev.backend` has it) and all six still define `NEXT_PUBLIC_JWT_SECRET`; deployment must supply the secret.

##### 2.1.1.1 Sub-feature: Token refresh and rotation

- **Status:** Active
- **What it does:** `POST /auth/refresh-token` validates the expired access token's signature (lifetime ignored), finds the user by its `email` claim, re-checks confirmed and active, then either rotates (current refresh token) or reissues only an access token (previous refresh token inside a 60 s grace window).
- **User flow:**
  1. Web NextAuth `jwt` callback runs on every session read; when `accessTokenExpiry` is within `REFRESH_WINDOW_MS` (10 min) it calls `refreshAccessToken`.
  2. `refreshesInFlight` map keeps one refresh per refresh token in the Next.js server process.
  3. Backend accepts the current token (`RefreshToken` matches and not expired) and rotates: `PreviousRefreshToken = old`, `RefreshTokenRotatedOn = now`, new token and expiry.
  4. A request carrying the previous token within 60 s (`RefreshTokenReuseGracePeriod`) gets a new access token plus the current refresh token, with no rotation, so parallel tabs converge.
  5. Any failure sets `token.error = "RefreshAccessTokenError"`; later reads skip refreshing; the client signs out once (2.1.1.3).
- **Business rules:** response shape equals login (`tokenInfo.*`); a missing `tokenInfo.token` is treated as failure. Invalid signature or malformed token: 400 `RefreshToken` "Invalid refresh token."; non-HS256 header: `UnauthorizedException`.
- **Errors & edge cases:** an inactive or unverified user cannot refresh (400). A refresh does not re-check the ADMIN role, so an admin session keeps refreshing after the role is removed (the permission cache still limits it to 10 minutes, 2.1.6.3).
- **Gotchas / tech debt:** The web refresh window (10 min) means a server component's `getServerSession` can rotate the token without writing the new refresh token back to the cookie; the next client read then relies on the 60 s grace window. Admin documents the same failure and shrank its buffer to 60 s (`caboodle.admin/src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/options.ts`, comment "IAM 01 AF2"). Not verified at runtime for web; see questions.

##### 2.1.1.2 Sub-feature: Logout and refresh-token revocation

- **Status:** Active
- **What it does:** Revokes the refresh token server-side, then ends the NextAuth session and clears per-person browser state.
- **User flow:**
  1. User picks Log out (workspace panel); `caboodle.web/src/helper/logOut.helper.ts` `logOutFn` calls `AccessService.logout()` (`POST /api/v1/auth/logout`, `caboodle.web/src/service/access.service.ts`), ignoring failure.
  2. Then `signOut({ callbackUrl })`, `clearAllCookies()`, `clearSignedInState()` (removes `cb-cmp-store`, `cb-cmp-store-userRole`, the selected-organization key), `setAccessToken(null)`.
  3. Backend `TokenService.LogoutAsync` nulls `RefreshToken`, `PreviousRefreshToken`, `RefreshTokenRotatedOn`, sets `RefreshTokenExpiryTime = now`, audits `auth.logout`; an unknown user id is a no-op 204.
- **Business rules:** the access token stays valid until it expires (no server-side access-token revocation list). `cb-cmp-store-navMode` deliberately survives logout.
- **Tests:** `caboodle.web/src/__tests__/helper/logOutNavPreference.test.ts` (7); backend `TokenServiceTests.LogoutClearsTheRefreshTokensAndIsAudited`.

##### 2.1.1.3 Sub-feature: Web token holder and 401 handling

- **Status:** Active
- **What it does:** Makes the current access token readable outside React and recovers from an expired token once before signing out.
- **User flow:**
  1. `SessionTokenSync` (mounted under `AuthProvider` in the root layout) writes `session.accessToken` into `caboodle.web/src/httpClient/sessionToken.ts` during render; route-group layouts also seed it from the server session through `AxiosInterceptor({ session })`.
  2. `applyRequestHeaders` adds `Authorization: Bearer` (and `OrganizationID`, owned by 2.2) to every axios request.
  3. On 401: `refreshAccessToken()` calls `getSession()` once (single flight); if a different token comes back the request is replayed once with `_retriedAfterRefresh`; otherwise `endSession()` signs out. 403 never signs out.
  4. When `session.error === "RefreshAccessTokenError"`, `SessionTokenSync` clears the token and calls `signOut({ callbackUrl: "/" })` once.
- **Code map:**

| Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `caboodle.web/src/components/SessionTokenSync.tsx` | Token write during render; one-time sign-out on refresh error |
| `caboodle.web/src/httpClient/sessionToken.ts` | `getAccessToken` / `setAccessToken` module variable |
| `caboodle.web/src/components/AxiosInterceptor.tsx` | `applyRequestHeaders`, `handleResponseError`, `refreshAccessToken`, `endSession`, `AxiosInterceptor` seeding shell |

- **Tests:** `caboodle.web/src/__tests__/components/AxiosInterceptor.test.tsx` (14), `caboodle.web/src/__tests__/helper/apiHeaders.test.ts` (12). Gap: `SessionTokenSync` has no direct test.
- **Gotchas / tech debt:** `sessionToken.ts` is a module-level variable and `AxiosInterceptor` (a client component) seeds it during render, which also runs during server-side rendering; whether the Next.js server process then shares one token across requests (and attaches it to server-side axios calls such as the NextAuth `login`) is not verified. See questions.

##### 2.1.1.4 Sub-feature: Master password sign-in

- **Status:** Feature-flagged (`SecuritySettings:MasterPassword` in appsettings; present in Development, Staging and Production)
- **What it does:** Any account (app or admin portal) signs in with the configured master password instead of its own; the email-confirmed, active and admin checks still apply.
- **Business rules:** compared with `!=` before `CheckPasswordAsync` (`TokenService.GetSignInFailureAsync`); when the setting is absent the comparison never matches.
- **Gotchas / tech debt:** a shared secret that opens every account, including Platform Admins, stored in the checked-in production appsettings file; successful master-password logins are audited as normal `auth.login_succeeded` with no marker.

##### 2.1.1.5 Sub-feature: Azure AD bearer authentication

- **Status:** Feature-flagged (`SecuritySettings:Provider` = `Jwt` in all environment appsettings, so the Azure AD branch is not active)
- **What it does:** When `Provider` is `AzureAd`, `AddAzureAdAuth` validates Microsoft identity tokens and `AzureAdJwtBearerEvents` calls `UserService.GetOrCreateFromPrincipalAsync`, which finds the user by `ObjectId` or creates or links one by UPN and display name, and adds the token's role if that role exists.

|---|---|

| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure/Auth/AzureAd/AzureAdJwtBearerEvents.cs` | Issuer check and user provisioning |

#### 2.1.2 Feature: Sign-up and email verification

- **Status:** Active
- **What it does:** Anyone can create an account with first name, last name, email (also used as user name), phone and password. A self sign-up starts inactive and unverified with the `UNASSIGNED` role, receives a 6-digit code by email, and becomes verified and active once the code is entered; it then logs in and continues to onboarding (company discovery, owned by the organizations module). An invited sign-up (link from an invitation email) creates a verified, active account and joins the inviting company in the same request.
- **User flow:**
  1. `/signup` (`caboodle.web/src/components/Auth/SignUpForm.tsx`): fields first name, last name, email (disabled when `?email=` is present), password, confirm password, terms checkbox (submit disabled until ticked). `userName` is sent as the email.
  2. Self sign-up: `POST /api/v1/registration` with `hasInvited: false` → `UserService.SignUpAsync` creates the user (`IsActive = false`, `EmailConfirmed = false`), adds `UNASSIGNED`, sends the code (2.1.2.1), answers `{ message }` only (no token).
  3. The web toasts "Check your email" and routes to `/verify-email?email=` (`verifyEmailCodeRoute`), which renders `VerifyEmailCode`.
  4. The person types the 6 digits (antd `Input.OTP`) → `POST /api/v1/users/verify-email-otp` → success toast and `/login?verified=1`.
  5. Resend button → `POST /api/v1/users/resend-email-verification` (client shows a 30 s countdown; the server answers 200 even when it sends nothing).
  6. A later login with a correct password and an unverified email also resends a code and opens the code screen (2.1.1).
  7. Invited sign-up: see 2.1.2.3. Signing up again over an unverified self sign-up: see 2.1.2.4.
- **Code map:**

| Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/Hosts/API/Controllers/Registration/RegistrationController.cs` | `POST /registration`: invited branch when `HasInvited && VerificationCode` else `SignUpAsync` |
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure/Identity/UserService.CreateUpdate.cs` | `SignUpAsync`, `CreateInvitedUserAsync`, `CreateVerifiedUserAsync`, `ConstructApplicationUser`, `AddRoleToInvitedUser`, `DefineUserHierarchyAsync` |
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure/Identity/UserService.Verification.cs` | `ResendEmailVerificationAsync`, `VerifyEmailOtpAsync`, `ActivateSelfSignUpAsync`, `CanReplaceUnverifiedSignUpAsync`, `ReplaceUnverifiedSignUpAsync` |
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure/Identity/UserService.Confirm.cs` | `ConfirmEmailAsync` (legacy link), unused `ConfirmPhoneNumberAsync` |
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure/Identity/SignupVerificationService.cs` | Chooses link, code or both per `OtpSettings.SignupMode`; sends the email; audits outcomes |
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure/Identity/VerificationCodeService.cs` | Issue (cooldown, invalidate previous, insert HMAC hash), verify (atomic attempt count, constant-time compare, lock at max) |
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure/Identity/OtpSettings.cs` | Settings and startup validation (HMAC key required for code modes) |
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Core/Application/Identity/Users/UserRegistrationRequest.cs` | Request and validator |
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Core/Application/Identity/Users/VerifyEmailOtpRequest.cs`, `VerifyEmailRequest.cs`, `UserEmailVerificationRequest.cs` | Verification requests and validators |
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/Database/Migrator/Migrations/Templates/SignupVerificationCodeEmailTemplate.cs` | Email template "Signup Verification Code" (EmailModule 14), seeded by `20261007143226_AddVerificationCodes.cs` |
| `caboodle.web/src/app/(auth)/signup/page.tsx`, `caboodle.web/src/components/Auth/SignUpForm.tsx` | Sign-up page; self vs invited branches |
| `caboodle.web/src/app/(auth)/verify-email/page.tsx`, `caboodle.web/src/components/Auth/VerifyEmail.tsx` | `?email=` alone → code screen; `?code=&email=` → legacy link flow |
| `caboodle.web/src/components/Auth/VerifyEmailCode.tsx` | 6-digit entry, resend with countdown |
| `caboodle.web/src/components/Auth/EmailSent.tsx`, `ActivateAccountMessage.tsx`, `InvitationPreviewCard.tsx` | Confirmation panels; invitation preview |
| `caboodle.web/src/helper/verificationCode.helper.ts` | Code length 6, 10 min, 5 tries, 30 s cooldown, `verifyEmailCodeRoute` |
| `caboodle.web/src/service/auth.service.ts` | `signup`, `verifyEmail`, `verifyEmailOtp`, `resendEmailVerification` |
| `caboodle.web/src/models/auth.interface.ts` | `ISignUp`, `IVerifyEmail`, `IVerifyEmailOtp`, `ISignUpResponse` |

- **Data:** `Identity.Users` (`IsActive`, `EmailConfirmed`, `EmailVerificationCode`, `EmailExpiryTime`), `Identity.UserRoles` (`UNASSIGNED`), `Identity.VerificationCodes`, `Identity.InvitedUsers` (legacy), `Organization.Invitations` (owned elsewhere).
- **APIs/interfaces:**

| Method | Path | Access rule | Request / Response | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | /api/v1/registration | `AllowAnonymous` | `UserRegistrationRequest { FirstName, LastName, Email, UserName, Password, ConfirmPassword, PhoneNumber, VerificationCode?, HasInvited }` / self: `ResponseMetaDTO { message }`; invited: `UserCreateResponseDTO { id, firstName, lastName, userName, email, phoneNumber, isActive, emailConfirmed }` (web `ISignUp` / `ISignUpResponse`) | `RegistrationController.RegisterAccountAsync` → `RegisterInvitedUserRequest` or `UserService.CreateInvitedUserAsync` or `UserService.SignUpAsync` |
| POST | /api/v1/users/verify-email-otp | `AllowAnonymous` | `VerifyEmailOtpRequest { Email, Code }` (code `^[0-9]{6}$`) / `ResponseMetaDTO` | `UsersController.ConfirmEmailWithCodeAsync` → `UserService.VerifyEmailOtpAsync` |
| POST | /api/v1/users/resend-email-verification | `AllowAnonymous` | `UserEmailVerificationRequest { Email }` / `ResponseMetaDTO` (always 200) | `UsersController.ResendConfirmEmailAsync` → `UserService.ResendEmailVerificationAsync` |
| POST | /api/v1/users/verify-email | `AllowAnonymous` | `VerifyEmailRequest { Email, Code: Guid }` / `ResponseMetaDTO` | `UsersController.ConfirmEmailAsync` → `UserService.ConfirmEmailAsync` (2.1.2.2) |

  Emails: "Signup Verification Code" (`IMailService.SendSignupVerificationCodeEmailAsync`, subject "Your Caboodle verification code: $CODE$", placeholders `$CODE$`, `$MINUTES$`, `$LINKBLOCK$`); legacy link email `SendEmailVerifyEmail`. Audit: `verification.sent`, `verification.succeeded`, `verification.failed`, `verification.locked` (metadata `Purpose`, `Attempts` or `Mode`; the code is never logged).
- **Business rules:**
  - `OtpSettings` in Development, Staging and Production: `SignupMode: Code`, `CodeLifetimeMinutes: 10`, `MaxAttempts: 5`, `ResendCooldownSeconds: 30`, `UnverifiedRetentionDays: 7`, `AllowUnverifiedReplacement: true`, `ActivateOnVerification: true`. Code default for `SignupMode` is `Link` when unset.
  - Startup throws when a code mode has no `OtpSettings:HmacKey` (`OtpSettings.Validate`).
  - Code = `RandomNumberGenerator.GetInt32(0, 1_000_000)` zero-padded to 6; stored as HMAC-SHA256 of `{userId}:{purpose}:{code}`.
  - Issuing a new code invalidates every active code for that user and purpose; within the cooldown no code is issued and the endpoint still answers 200.
  - Verification counts the attempt atomically before comparing (`CountAttemptSql`), so parallel guesses cannot exceed `MaxAttempts`; on the 5th wrong try the code is invalidated (`Locked`).
  - Unknown email, already verified, wrong, expired or locked code all answer 400 `Code` "Invalid or expired code." (enumeration-safe).
  - `ActivateOnVerification`: verifying sets `IsActive = true` only when every role of the account is `UNASSIGNED`; accounts holding a legacy business role stay inactive until an admin activates them.
  - Validators: email format, user name min 3, first and last name required, password min 6, confirm must equal password.
- **Dependencies:** 2.2 IAM audit; organizations module (invitations, discovery after login); email service; `AppUrls:BaseUrl` for links.
- **Errors & edge cases:**
  - Duplicate email that cannot be replaced: 400 `Invalid Email` "User with {email} is already in use. Try with another email." (reveals that the account exists).
  - Duplicate user name: 400 `Invalid Username`.
  - `SignUpAsync` returns the "code sent" message even when `UserManager.CreateAsync` fails (no error raised); the person waits for a code that never comes.
- **Tests:** backend `caboodle.backend/caboodle/tests/Infrastructure.Test/Identity/SignupVerificationTests.cs` (13), `VerificationCodeServiceTests.cs` (7), `CreateInvitedUserAsyncTests.cs` (4), `CreateVerifiedUserAsyncTests.cs` (2), `PasswordConfirmationValidatorTests.cs` (2); web `caboodle.web/src/__tests__/components/Auth/SignUpForm.test.tsx` (5), `VerifyEmail.test.tsx` (3), `VerifyEmailCode.test.tsx` (5), `caboodle.web/src/__tests__/helper/verificationCode.helper.test.ts` (3). Gap: no backend test for the silent `SignUpAsync` create failure.
- **Gotchas / tech debt:** No rate limiting beyond the per-code attempt limit and resend cooldown (no IP throttling on sign-up, login, verify or resend). `VerificationPurpose.EmailChange` exists with no caller (no email-change feature).

##### 2.1.2.1 Sub-feature: 6-digit code verification

- **Status:** Active (`OtpSettings:SignupMode = Code` in all environments)
- **What it does:** Issues, emails, checks and expires one-time sign-up codes stored hashed in `Identity.VerificationCodes`.
- **User flow:** sign-up or resend → `SignupVerificationService.SendAsync` → `VerificationCodeService.IssueAsync` (null inside cooldown) → email; entry → `VerifyEmailOtpAsync` → `SignupVerificationService.VerifyAsync` → `EmailConfirmed = true` and maybe `IsActive = true`.
- **Tests:** `VerificationCodeServiceTests.cs`, `SignupVerificationTests.cs`.

##### 2.1.2.2 Sub-feature: Legacy link verification

- **Status:** Feature-flagged (link emails are only sent when `OtpSettings:SignupMode` is `Link` or `LinkAndCode`; all environments use `Code`. The endpoint and web page still verify links issued earlier.)
- **What it does:** `POST /users/verify-email` compares the GUID in the link with `Identity.Users.EmailVerificationCode` and `EmailExpiryTime` (`SecuritySettings:EmailVerificationCodeExpiredInMinutes` = 7200, 5 days). Web `VerifyEmailLink` (`caboodle.web/src/components/Auth/VerifyEmail.tsx`) runs it when `?code=&email=` are both present and offers "Resend Verification Link" on failure.
- **Business rules:** unknown email 404; already verified 400 `User`; wrong or expired code 400 `Code` "Code is invalid or expired."; success also runs `ActivateSelfSignUpAsync`. Resend renews an expired link only when `SendsLink` is true.
- **Gotchas / tech debt:** unlike the code endpoint this one is not enumeration-safe (404 vs 400). In Code mode the "Resend Verification Link" button sends a code, not a link.

##### 2.1.2.3 Sub-feature: Invited sign-up

- **Status:** Active (organization invitations); legacy `Identity.InvitedUsers` branch Deprecated (new legacy invitations are created only by hidden admin pages, 2.1.5.5)
- **What it does:** Registration with `HasInvited: true` and a `VerificationCode` first looks the code up in `Organization.Invitations` (`RegisterInvitedUserRequest`, includes legacy codes migrated by the organization backfill). If found it creates a verified, active `UNASSIGNED` account (`CreateVerifiedUserAsync`) and accepts the invitation in one transaction, deleting any matching `Identity.InvitedUsers` row. If not found the legacy `CreateInvitedUserAsync` path runs.
- **User flow:**
  1. Invitation email links to `/signup?code={token}&email=`; the web shows "Accept your invitation" and `InvitationPreviewCard` (`GET /invitations/{token}`, owned by the organizations module).
  2. Submit sends `verificationCode` and `hasInvited: true`.
  3. If the response is active and confirmed, the web signs in with the typed password and routes to `/dashboard` (fallback `/login`).
  4. If the email already has an account: 400 `Invitation Already Accepted` "An account with this email already exists. Log in to accept the invitation." The web routes to `/login?invite={token}&email=`, and login then opens `/invitations/{token}`.
  5. Legacy path: account created with `EmailConfirmed = true`, `IsActive` true only when the inviter was an ADMIN; the web shows `ActivateAccountMessage` ("The Admin needs to activate your account...") when inactive.
- **Business rules (legacy path, `UserService.CreateInvitedUserAsync`):** invitation must exist and not be soft-deleted ("Invitation Cancelled" when it was), not expired (`SecuritySettings:InvitedUserCodeExpiredInMinutes` = 7200); a BrandOwner invitation fails when the brand already has an owner; on success `AddRoleToInvitedUser` assigns `BRANDSUBUSER` + `Brand.BrandSubUsers` row, `BRANDOWNER` + `Brand.Brands.UserID`, `BROKER` / `BROKERSUBUSER` + `Brand.BrandBrokers` rows, or `UNASSIGNED`; `DefineUserHierarchyAsync` writes `Identity.UsersHierarchy`; the invitation row is hard-deleted.
- **Errors & edge cases:** an invited address that already has an unverified self sign-up gets the "already exists" 400 but cannot log in until it finishes the code flow (no replacement on the invitation path). The account is created before the invitation accept transaction; if accepting fails the person can log in and accept via `POST /invitations/{token}/accept`.
- **Tests:** `CreateInvitedUserAsyncTests.cs`, `CreateVerifiedUserAsyncTests.cs`, `caboodle.backend/caboodle/tests/Organization.Application.Test/Invitations/InvitationRequestTests.cs`.
- **Gotchas / tech debt:** `GetBrokerInsertQuery` / `GetSubBrokerInsertQuery` build SQL by string interpolation of GUIDs and `DateTime.UtcNow`; values are server-generated, but the format depends on server culture.

##### 2.1.2.4 Sub-feature: Unverified sign-up replacement

- **Status:** Active (`OtpSettings:AllowUnverifiedReplacement = true`)
- **What it does:** Signing up again with an email whose account is unverified, holds only `UNASSIGNED`, and has no `Organization.Memberships` row replaces that account's name, phone, user name and password and sends a new code, instead of failing as a duplicate.
- **Business rules:** user name taken by another account → 400 `Invalid Username`; Identity errors → 400 `Registration`. A verified account or one with access is never replaced.
- **Tests:** `SignupVerificationTests.ReRegistrationReplacesAnUnverifiedSelfSignUp`, `AccountsWithAccessOrVerifiedEmailsAreNeverReplaced`, `ReplacementRefusesAUserNameTakenBySomeoneElseAndIdentityErrors`.

##### 2.1.2.5 Sub-feature: Unverified-account cleanup job

- **Status:** Active
- **What it does:** Hangfire recurring job `unverified-account-cleanup-daily` (cron `30 2 * * *`, UTC) deletes abandoned self sign-ups and old codes.
- **User flow:**
  1. `UnverifiedAccountCleanupJobRegistrar` (hosted service, `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/Modules/Admin/Modules.Admin.Application/Startup.cs`) registers the job on application start.
  2. `UnverifiedAccountCleanupJobExecutor.ExecuteAsync` selects users with `EmailConfirmed = false`, at least one `SignupEmail` code, no code newer than `UnverifiedRetentionDays` (7), no role other than `UNASSIGNED`, and no membership row (any status).
  3. Deletes them through `IUserService.DeleteAsync` → `UserAccountDeletion` (2.1.5.4), then deletes all `Identity.VerificationCodes` older than 30 days (`CodeRetentionDays`).
- **Code map:**

| Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/Modules/Admin/Modules.Admin.Application/Verification/UnverifiedAccountCleanupJobRegistrar.cs` | Job id, cron, registration |
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/Modules/Admin/Modules.Admin.Application/Verification/UnverifiedAccountCleanupJobExecutor.cs` | Selection SQL, delete, code purge, log |

- **Business rules:** legacy accounts (no codes) and admin-created accounts are never touched.
- **Tests:** `caboodle.backend/caboodle/tests/Admin.Application.Test/Verification/UnverifiedAccountCleanupJobExecutorTests.cs` (3).
- **Gotchas / tech debt:** `UserAccountDeletion` refuses the whole batch when any one account fails a guard, so one bad row would stop every deletion in that run (the selection excludes admins and members, which makes this unlikely).

#### 2.1.3 Feature: Password reset

- **Status:** Active
- **What it does:** A person who forgot the password requests an emailed link carrying an ASP.NET Identity reset token, then sets a new password. Anonymous; available to every account whose email is confirmed.
- **User flow:**
  1. `/forgot-password` (`caboodle.web/src/components/Auth/ForgotPassword.tsx`) → `POST /api/v1/users/forgot-password` → `EmailSent` panel.
  2. Backend sends the email only when the account exists and its email is confirmed; the answer is always "If an account exists for this email, a link to reset your password has been sent."
  3. Link `{AppUrls:BaseUrl}/reset-password?code={escaped token}&email={escaped email}`.
  4. `/reset-password` (`caboodle.web/src/components/Auth/ResetPassword.tsx`): new password + confirm (must match) → `POST /api/v1/users/reset-password` → success → `/login`.
  5. A signed-in person who opens the link is logged out first by `caboodle.web/src/app/(auth)/layout.tsx` (any `?code=` other than an invitation).
- **Code map:**

| Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure/Identity/UserService.Password.cs` | `ForgotPasswordAsync`, `ResetPasswordAsync`, `ChangePasswordAsync` |
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Core/Application/Identity/Users/Password/ForgotPasswordRequest.cs`, `ResetPasswordRequest.cs` | Requests (forgot has an email validator; reset has none) |
| `caboodle.web/src/app/(auth)/forgot-password/page.tsx`, `caboodle.web/src/components/Auth/ForgotPassword.tsx` | Request form |
| `caboodle.web/src/app/(auth)/reset-password/page.tsx`, `caboodle.web/src/components/Auth/ResetPassword.tsx` | New password form; `replaceSpaceWithPlus` restores `+` in the token |
| `caboodle.web/src/service/auth.service.ts` | `requestResetPassword`, `resetPassword` |

- **Data:** reset tokens are not stored by the app (Identity data-protection token on `Identity.Users.SecurityStamp`).
- **APIs/interfaces:**

| Method | Path | Access rule | Request / Response | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | /api/v1/users/forgot-password | `AllowAnonymous` | `ForgotPasswordRequest { Email }` / `ResponseMetaDTO` (same text always) | `UsersController.ForgotPasswordAsync` → `UserService.ForgotPasswordAsync` |
| POST | /api/v1/users/reset-password | `AllowAnonymous` | `ResetPasswordRequest { Email, Password, Token }` (web `IResetPassword`) / `ResponseMetaDTO` "Password Reset Successful!" | `UsersController.ResetPasswordAsync` → `UserService.ResetPasswordAsync` |

  Email: `IMailService.SendResetPasswordEmail(name, email, link)`.
- **Business rules:** Identity password rules (min 6, no complexity). Token lifetime is the Identity default; no `DataProtectionTokenProviderOptions` is configured in code.
- **Dependencies:** email service; `AppUrls:BaseUrl`.
- **Errors & edge cases:** reset with an unknown email returns 404 `User` "User not found" (forgot-password is enumeration-safe, reset is not); Identity errors are joined into 400 `ResetPassword`.
- **Tests:** `caboodle.backend/caboodle/tests/Infrastructure.Test/Identity/UserServicePasswordTests.cs` (2: same answer for unknown email, URL encoding). Gaps: reset path untested; no web tests for `ForgotPassword` or `ResetPassword`.
- **Gotchas / tech debt:** a reset does not revoke the refresh token, so existing sessions keep refreshing for up to 14 days.

#### 2.1.4 Feature: User profile

- **Status:** Active
- **What it does:** The signed-in person views and edits their own name and phone, uploads or removes a profile photo, and changes their password at `/profile` in the customer web app. Role badges on the page come from `/me/access` (2.2). Any authenticated user (`[Authorize]`), any organization type.
- **User flow:**
  1. `/profile` (`caboodle.web/src/app/(brand)/profile/page.tsx`, under the session-checked `(brand)` layout) loads `GET /api/v1/profile` via `useGetUserProfile` (enabled once `session.accessToken` exists).
  2. Tabs "General Information" and "Security" (accessible tablist; both panels stay mounted).
  3. General: Edit → `PUT /api/v1/profile` with first name, last name, phone → toast, refetch.
  4. Photo: Change → client check (`validateProfileImage`: PNG or JPG, max 5 MB) → `PUT /api/v1/profile/image-upload` (multipart, field `ProfileImage`); Remove (Popconfirm) → `DELETE /api/v1/profile/image-remove`.
  5. Security: current, new, confirm password with an advisory strength meter (`describePasswordStrength`) → `PUT /api/v1/profile/change-password` → toast and form reset.
- **Code map:**

| Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/Hosts/API/Controllers/Profile/ProfileController.cs` | Six profile endpoints; each returns 401 when the user id claim is missing |
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure/Identity/UserService.CreateUpdate.cs` | `UpdateAsync`, `UploadProfileImageAsync`, `DeleteProfileImageAsync` |
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure/Identity/UserService.Password.cs` | `ChangePasswordAsync` |
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure/Identity/UserService.Permissions.cs` | `GetPermissionsAsync` |
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure/FileStorage/AwsS3StorageService.cs` | `UploadProfileImageAsync`: key `Users/{userId}/ProfileImages/{guid}{ext}`, returns a pre-signed URL |
| `caboodle.web/src/app/(brand)/profile/page.tsx` | Page, identity card, tabs, photo upload (direct `axios.put`), forms |
| `caboodle.web/src/service/profile.service.ts` | `getUser`, `updateUser`, `changeUserPassword`, `removeProfileImage` |
| `caboodle.web/src/hooks/profile.ts` | `useGetUserProfile`, `useUpdateUserProfile`, `useUpdateChangePassword`, `useRemoveProfileImage` (`QueryKeys.getProfile`) |
| `caboodle.web/src/helper/profile.helper.ts` | Display name, initials, role badges from `/me/access`, `validateProfileImage`, `describePasswordStrength` |
| `caboodle.web/src/models/genericModel.ts` | `IProfile` |

- **Data:** `Identity.Users` (`FirstName`, `LastName`, `PhoneNumber`, `ImageUrl`, `PasswordHash`); S3 object under `Users/{userId}/ProfileImages/`.
- **APIs/interfaces:**

| Method | Path | Access rule | Request / Response | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | /api/v1/profile | `Authorize` | none / `UserDetailsDto { id, userName, firstName, lastName, email, isActive, emailConfirmed, phoneNumber, imageUrl }` (web `IProfile`) | `ProfileController.GetProfileAsync` → `UserService.GetAsync` |
| PUT | /api/v1/profile | `Authorize` | `UpdateUserRequest { Id, FirstName, LastName, PhoneNumber }` (names max 75) / `UserDetailsDto` | `ProfileController.UpdateProfileAsync` → `UserService.UpdateAsync(request, callerId)` |
| PUT | /api/v1/profile/image-upload | `Authorize` | multipart `UserProfileImageUploadRequest { ProfileImage: IFormFile }` / `UserDetailsDto` | `ProfileController.UploadProfileImageAsync` → `UserService.UploadProfileImageAsync` |
| DELETE | /api/v1/profile/image-remove | `Authorize` | none / `UserDetailsDto` | `ProfileController.RemoveProfileImageAsync` → `UserService.DeleteProfileImageAsync` |
| PUT | /api/v1/profile/change-password | `Authorize` | `ChangePasswordRequest { Password, NewPassword, ConfirmNewPassword }` / `ResponseMetaDTO` | `ProfileController.ChangePasswordAsync` → `UserService.ChangePasswordAsync` |
| GET | /api/v1/profile/permissions | `Authorize` | none / `List<string>` permission names | `ProfileController.GetPermissionsAsync` → `UserService.GetPermissionsAsync` (2.1.4.2) |

  Events: `ApplicationUserUpdatedEvent` published on update and image changes. S3: upload, and `IFileStorageService.Remove` of the previous image.
- **Business rules:** the profile update always targets the caller's id (the body `Id` is ignored); `UpdateAsync` calls `SignInManager.RefreshSignInAsync` (cookie sign-in refresh, no effect on JWT). Server-side image check: extension must be in `FileType.Image` (`.jpg,.png,.jpeg`); the old image is removed from S3 before the new upload. Change password: old password must match (Identity), new must equal confirm (validator).
- **Dependencies:** AWS S3 (`IFileStorageService`); 2.2 `/me/access` for role badges; the persisted `HeaderWithBack` shell.
- **Errors & edge cases:** change password failure is a generic 400 `Password` "Change password failed." (Identity reasons dropped). Removing when there is no image answers 200 with the unchanged user.
- **Tests:** web `caboodle.web/src/__tests__/app/ProfilePage.test.tsx` (15), `caboodle.web/src/__tests__/helper/profile.helper.test.ts` (27). Backend: none for profile endpoints.
- **Gotchas / tech debt:**
  - The stored `ImageUrl` is an S3 pre-signed URL valid for 20 years (`AwsS3StorageService.GetFileUrl`, `Expires = DateTime.Now.AddYears(20)`), and it is also copied into the JWT `image_url` claim.
  - `useUpdateUserProfile.onError` reads `error.response.data.error.messages`, but the web interceptor rejects with `error.response` itself, so `messagesObj` is `undefined` and `Object.keys(undefined)` throws instead of showing the server message (`caboodle.web/src/hooks/profile.ts`).
  - The photo upload bypasses the shared axios instance and sends `authorization: bearer {session.accessToken}` directly, so it gets no 401 refresh-and-retry.
  - `ProfileService.getUser` takes the token as an argument instead of relying on the interceptor; `hooks/profile.ts` imports `profile` from `console` and `use` from React, both unused.
  - Change password does not revoke refresh tokens.
  - The route lives in the `(brand)` route group, but the URL `/profile` serves brokers too.

#### 2.1.5 Feature: Platform user management (admin)

- **Status:** Active (accounts list and "Accounts Without a Company"); several legacy screens and endpoints are Deprecated or Partial (see sub-features)
- **What it does:** Platform Admins in `caboodle.admin` list every account, filter it, enable or disable it, delete accounts that belong to no company, open a person's memberships, add a person to a brand, and invite people (organization invitation dialog). Company roles are no longer set here; they are managed on the Members screens. All backend endpoints require `MustHavePermission(..., Users, User)`, which only the seeded `ADMIN` role holds (2.1.6).
- **User flow:**
  1. Sidebar "People & access" › "Accounts Without a Company" opens `/users-unassigned` (`caboodle.admin/src/component/Layout/Sidebar/navConfig.tsx`). `/all-users` has no sidebar entry; it is reached by URL or the "Open Users" button on a member page (`caboodle.admin/src/component/Membership/MemberDetail.tsx`) and highlights Members.
  2. Both pages render `UsersTable` (`caboodle.admin/src/component/User/UsersTable.tsx`): columns user name, account (Platform Admin tag), first and last name, email, active, email confirmed, phone; filter drawer (`AllUsersFilter`: name, email, phone, status, email confirmed, brand).
  3. Row actions: Memberships drawer (`UserMembershipsDrawer`, `GET /members?userId=`, remove a membership; owned elsewhere), Add to a brand (`AddUserToBrand` → `PUT /api/v1/brands/assign-user-to-brand`, owned elsewhere), Disable or Enable (`PUT /users/{id}/update-active-status/{status}`), Delete (`DELETE /users/delete-multiple` with one id; dialog explains the 409 rule).
  4. Header "Invite User" opens `InviteMember` (`POST /invitations`, organizations module), not the legacy invite.

  - `GET /users/unassigned` = no non-deleted `Organization.Memberships` row and not a Platform Admin (`ADMIN` role), excluding the caller.
  - Status and email-confirmation changes are refused for ADMIN accounts (400 `Admin`).

  - `GET /users` declares `ProducesResponseType(PagedData<UserDetailsDto>)` but returns `PagedData<UserListDto>`.
  - `sortingOrder` is applied to first name only; other columns cannot be sorted server-side.
  - `getAllUserList` builds the query string with `getFilterParamString`; `getAllUsers` and `getAllUnassignedUsers` use axios `params`, two styles for the same endpoint family.
  - `UserService.exportUser` (`caboodle.admin/src/services/users.service.ts`) calls `GET /api/v1/masterdataupload/users`, a route `MasterDataUploadController` does not define, and has no caller (dead code).

##### 2.1.5.3 Sub-feature: Activation and email-confirmation status

- **Status:** Active for activation (UsersTable Disable/Enable); email-confirmation endpoint Partial (no caller in either frontend)
- **What it does:** Sets `Identity.Users.IsActive` (sends the status email) or `EmailConfirmed` (no email). An inactive account cannot log in or refresh (2.1.1).
- **Gotchas / tech debt:** deactivation does not revoke the refresh token or the current access token; the next refresh fails, so a deactivated person keeps API access until the access token expires (up to 24 h).

##### 2.1.5.4 Sub-feature: Guarded account deletion

- **Status:** Active
- **What it does:** `UserAccountDeletion.DeleteAsync` deletes accounts in one transaction after checks; used by `DELETE /users/delete-multiple`, `DELETE /users/delete` and the cleanup job (2.1.2.5).
- **Business rules:** empty list → 400 `Users`; any unknown id → 404 for the whole batch; the caller's own id → 409; any Platform Admin → 409; any account with a non-deleted membership → 409 naming each person and company ("Remove X from Y first (Members)."). On success: pending access requests soft-deleted, verification codes deleted, legacy links cleared (`Brand.Brands.UserID = NULL`, `BrandBrokers` and `BrandSubUsers` soft-deleted), `Identity.Users` row hard-deleted, one `user.deleted` audit per account with `RefreshUserIds`.
- **Gotchas / tech debt:** two endpoints do the same thing with different body keys (`usersID` vs `userIDs`); only `delete-multiple` has a frontend caller. `Identity.UsersHierarchy` and `Identity.InvitedUsers` rows created by the deleted person are not cleaned up (not in `UserAccountSql.DeleteAccounts`).

##### 2.1.5.5 Sub-feature: Legacy user invitation

- **Status:** Deprecated (`/invite-user` redirects to `/invitations`; `/invited-users` and the `InviteUser` form are reachable only by URL and have no sidebar entry; `invite/brand-sub-user` and `invited-user/{code}` have no frontend caller)
- **What it does:** Creates or refreshes an `Identity.InvitedUsers` row (`VerificationCode`, 5-day expiry) and emails `{AppUrls:BaseUrl}/signup?code=&email=`; accepted through 2.1.2.3 (legacy path). Admin `/invited-users` lists them (`GET /subusers/admin/invited-users`), resends (`POST /users/invite/{id}`) and cancels (`DELETE /subusers/cancel-invitation`, 2.1.7.4).
- **APIs/interfaces:**

| Method | Path | Access rule | Request / Response | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | /api/v1/users/invite | `MustHavePermission(Create, Users, User)` | `CreateInviteUserRequest { Email, UserType, BrandIDs, ParentUserID? }` / `ResponseMetaDTO` | `UsersController.InviteAsync` → `UserService.InviteAsync` |
| POST | /api/v1/users/invite/{id} | `MustHavePermission(Update, Users, User)` | path invited-user id / `ResponseMetaDTO` | `UsersController.ReinviteAsync` → `UserService.ResendInvitaionLinkAsync` |
| POST | /api/v1/users/invite/brand-sub-user | `MustHavePermission(Create, Users, User)` + `BrandIDHeader` | `CreateBrandSubUserInviteReqest { Emails[] }` / `ResponseMetaDTO` | `UsersController.InviteBrandSubUserAsync` → `UserService.InviteBrandSubUserAsync` |
| GET | /api/v1/users/invited-user/{verificationCode} | `MustHavePermission(View, Users, User)` | path GUID / `InvitedUserDetailsDTO { Email, UserType, ParentUserID, ExpiryTime, Brands[] }` | `UsersController.GetInvitedUserByVerificationCodeAsync` → `UserService.GetInvitedUserByVerificationCodeAsync` |

- **Business rules (`UserService.CheckValidationForInvitedUser`):** email must not belong to an account; `UserType` must be defined; brand ids must exist; a BrandOwner invitation fails if the first brand already has an owner; a non-admin inviting a BrandSubUser must own the brand; a BrokerSubUser invitation requires `ParentUserID`. Resend is allowed for the creator or an admin (others get 404).
- **Gotchas / tech debt:**
  - `ValidateInvitedBrandSubUser` and `GetBrandNames` build `IN (...)` SQL by string interpolation; the brand-sub-user emails come from the request body, so `POST /users/invite/brand-sub-user` concatenates caller input into SQL (SQL injection risk; endpoint is admin-only and has no caller).
  - The BrokerSubUser check loads the broker's brands into `brands` and never uses them; it compares the request ids with themselves (`validBrands`), so the "does not belong to the Broker" error cannot fire.
  - A legacy invitation is not an `Organization.Invitations` row, so the web `InvitationPreviewCard` (`GET /invitations/{token}`) cannot preview it.

##### 2.1.5.7 Sub-feature: Direct account create, update and email check

- **Status:** Partial (endpoints built, no caller in `caboodle.web` or `caboodle.admin`)

#### 2.1.6 Feature: Legacy roles and platform permissions

- **Status:** Active for the `ADMIN` role and `MustHavePermission` platform permissions; the other legacy roles are Deprecated as an access model (still assigned by the legacy invitation path and still read by a few legacy code paths, listed below)
- **What it does:** Every account holds one or more ASP.NET Identity roles from `CaboodleRoles` (`ADMIN`, `UNASSIGNED`, `BRANDOWNER`, `BROKER`, `BRANDSUBUSER`, `BROKERSUBUSER`). Roles carry permission claims; `[MustHavePermission(action, resource, module)]` on an endpoint requires the caller's roles to hold `Permissions.{module}.{resource}.{action}`. Since the IAM work, company access is decided by organization membership (2.2 and the organizations module); in practice `MustHavePermission` now marks Platform Admin endpoints, and `ADMIN` is the Platform Admin.
- **User flow:**
  1. On startup `ApplicationDbSeeder.SeedRolesAsync` creates any missing default role and adds missing permission claims: all of `CaboodlePermissions.Admin` to ADMIN, `CaboodlePermissions.Broker` to BROKER, `CaboodlePermissions.SubBroker` to BROKERSUBUSER; BRANDOWNER, BRANDSUBUSER and UNASSIGNED get none.
  2. `SeedAdminUserAsync` creates `admin@caboodle.com` with the ADMIN role when it does not exist.
  3. A request to a `MustHavePermission` endpoint goes through `PermissionPolicyProvider` → `PermissionRequirement` → `PermissionAuthorizationHandler` → `UserService.HasPermissionAsync` (2.1.6.3).
  4. New accounts get only `UNASSIGNED` (sign-up, invited organization sign-up, admin create). Assigning roles through the API is refused (2.1.6.2).
- **Code map:**

| Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|

| GET | /api/v1/users/brands-info | `MustHavePermission(View, Users, User)` | query `userID`, `roleName` / `UserBrandsInfoDTO { BrandsInfo[], ParentBrokerID? }` | `UsersController.GetAssignedBrandsOfUserAsync` → `GetBrandsOfUserRequestHandler` |

  Events: `ApplicationRoleCreatedEvent`, `ApplicationRoleUpdatedEvent` (with `PermissionsUpdated`), `ApplicationRoleDeletedEvent`.
- **Business rules:**
  - Role list hides ADMIN always, hides UNASSIGNED unless `isUnassignedIncluded`, hides the two sub-user roles when `isSubExcluded`.
  - Default roles cannot be renamed or deleted (409); a role in use cannot be deleted (409). `UpdatePermissionsAsync` has no default-role guard, so ADMIN's permission set can be edited through the API.
  - `AssignRoleAsync` answers 404 for an unknown user or role, then always 400 `Role` "This role can't be assigned." (comment: Platform Admins are made by developers; company roles live under Members).
  - `RemoveRoleAsync` refuses UNASSIGNED (404 "Invalid role."), re-adds UNASSIGNED when the user ends with no role, and clears that user's permission cache.
  - Seeding only adds roles and claims; it never removes a permission that left the code lists.
- **Where legacy business roles still matter (verified readers):**
  - `ADMIN`: admin-portal login gate (`TokenService`), every `MustHavePermission` endpoint (only role seeded with those permissions), excluded from deletion and from status changes, excluded from the unassigned list, short-circuit in `BrandValidationMiddleware` and `CategoryReviewAccessHelper`.
  - `UNASSIGNED`: default role; `ActivateSelfSignUpAsync` and unverified replacement only act on UNASSIGNED-only accounts; the cleanup job only deletes them.
  - `BROKER` / `BROKERSUBUSER` / `BRANDSUBUSER` / `BRANDOWNER`: `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure/Middleware/BrandValidationMiddleware.cs` (which legacy brand table to check for the `BrandID` header before falling back to `IAccessContext`), `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/Modules/Broker/Modules.Broker.Application/Helper/CategoryReviewAccessHelper.cs` (brand side vs broker side), `GetMyAssignedBrandsRequest` (`GET /brands/me`, now `MustHavePermission(View, Users, User)`), `GetBrandsOfUserRequest`, legacy brand-broker assignment requests in `Modules/Brand/.../BrokerBrand/`, and the legacy sub-user handlers (2.1.7).
  - The seeded BROKER and BROKERSUBUSER permissions (module `Broker`) guard no reachable endpoint: the five controller actions that use a `Broker`-module permission (`BrokersController` GET, four `BrandReportController` status-option writes) require resources excluded from those role sets, so only ADMIN passes.
- **Dependencies:** `ICacheService`, `ICacheKeyService`; ASP.NET authorization; 2.2 (module and org-permission handlers share the policy provider).
- **Errors & edge cases:** `PermissionAuthorizationHandler` throws 401 when no user id is present; a missing permission becomes a 403 envelope via `AccessForbiddenResultHandler` (2.2).
- **Tests:** `caboodle.backend/caboodle/tests/Infrastructure.Test/Identity/UserServicePermissionCacheTests.cs` (3), `UserServiceLegacyEndpointsTests.cs` (assign-role refusal), `caboodle.backend/caboodle/tests/API.Test/Authorization/EndpointAuthorizationCoverageTests.cs` (every endpoint carries an authorization attribute; `RolesController` listed as a platform controller; `AuthController`, `UsersController`, `RegistrationController` as management controllers). No tests for `RoleService` or the seeder.
- **Gotchas / tech debt:**
  - The seeder creates `admin@caboodle.com` with a hard-coded weak password hashed at seed time (`ApplicationDbSeeder.SeedAdminUserAsync`) on any database where that email is missing.
  - `RoleService.UpdatePermissionsAsync` calls `SaveChangesAsync` once per added claim (no batching, no transaction).
  - `GetRolesAsync` returns `NormalizedName` as `RoleName`; `GET /users` returns the display `Name`; consumers compare against different spellings (`"Admin"` in admin `UsersTable`, `ADMIN` in middleware).
  - The admin app calls only `GET /roles` (from the deprecated `AddRoleToUser`), `users/brands-info` (hook `useGetUserBrands`) and the always-refused `assign-role`; the other role endpoints have no frontend caller.

##### 2.1.6.1 Sub-feature: Permission check and cache

- **Status:** Active
- **What it does:** `HasPermissionAsync` loads the caller's permission list from role claims and caches it; the stored `CachedOn` caps the age at 10 minutes even though the cache's own expiry slides.
- **Business rules:** invalidation on role-permission change (`InvalidateUserPermissionCacheHandler`) and on `RemoveRoleAsync`; nothing else invalidates it, so a changed role membership through other paths takes up to 10 minutes to apply.
- **Tests:** `UserServicePermissionCacheTests.cs`.

#### 2.1.7 Feature: Legacy sub-users

- **Status:** Deprecated (superseded by organization members and roles; the brand-owner and broker endpoints have no frontend caller, and the admin screens that use the admin endpoints are hidden from the sidebar and reachable by URL only)
- **What it does:** Before IAM, a brand owner or broker invited "sub-users" who were linked through `Brand.BrandSubUsers` or `Brand.BrandBrokers.ParentBrokerID` and `Identity.UsersHierarchy`. `SubUsersController` (route `api/v1/subusers`) lists, removes, activates and cancels those people and their pending `Identity.InvitedUsers` rows. Every endpoint is `MustHavePermission` on `SubUsers`/`SubUser` or `Users`/`User`, which only the `ADMIN` role holds, so brand owners and brokers can no longer call their own endpoints.

#### 2.1.8 Feature: Admin app authentication

- **Status:** Active
- **What it does:** `caboodle.admin` signs Platform Admins in through its own NextAuth credentials provider against `POST /api/v1/admin/login`, which adds an `ADMIN`-role check to the normal sign-in. It keeps the session alive with a proactive refresh timer, coordinates logout across tabs, and returns the user to the page they were on after a forced logout. Only accounts holding the `ADMIN` Identity role can sign in.
- **User flow:**
  1. `/` (`caboodle.admin/src/app/page.tsx`) redirects to `/dashboard` when a session without `RefreshAccessTokenError` exists, else `/login`.
  2. `/login` (`caboodle.admin/src/component/App/Authentication/Login.tsx`) calls `useAuth().login` → `signIn("credentials", { redirect: false })`.
  3. NextAuth `authorize` (`caboodle.admin/src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/options.ts`) → `AuthService.login` → `POST /api/v1/admin/login` → `TokenService.GetAdminTokenAsync` (portal `admin` in the audit entry).
  4. Failure: the `messages` object is forwarded as JSON; the form shows the first backend text (wrong password, "User not active.", "Email not confirmed.", or 401 `Generic` "You have no permission to access admin panel."), else a status-based fallback (429, 5xx, network).
  5. Success: broadcast `LOGIN`, then route to `?redirect=` (validated relative path), a stored post-login route, or `/dashboard`.
  6. `(mainApp)/layout.tsx` server-checks the session and treats `RefreshAccessTokenError` as signed out.
  7. Header logout (`caboodle.admin/src/component/Layout/AppHeader.tsx` → `useAuth().logout`): `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` (errors ignored), clear the token cache and storage keys, broadcast `LOGOUT`, `signOut({ redirect: false })`, hard navigation to `/login`.
- **Code map:**

| Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/Hosts/API/Controllers/Admin/AdminController.cs` | `POST admin/login` (only the Auth region belongs here) |
| `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure/Identity/TokenService.cs` | `GetAdminTokenAsync` (`requireAdmin`), shared refresh and logout |
| `caboodle.admin/src/app/(auth)/login/page.tsx`, `caboodle.admin/src/component/App/Authentication/Login.tsx` | Login page, error mapping, post-login routing |
| `caboodle.admin/src/app/page.tsx`, `caboodle.admin/src/app/(mainApp)/layout.tsx` | Server redirects and session gate |
| `caboodle.admin/src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/options.ts`, `route.ts` | Credentials provider, `jwt` callback (refresh on `update()` trigger, 60 s buffer, expired refresh token short-circuit), `maxAge` 14 days, `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` |
| `caboodle.admin/src/provider/AuthProvider.tsx` | `SessionProvider` with the server session, `AuthSessionWatcher` as sibling of children |
| `caboodle.admin/src/component/AuthSessionWatcher.tsx` | Token cache mirror, `update()` handle for the interceptor, refresh 30 s before expiry, refresh on tab focus, terminal-error logout, cross-tab handlers |
| `caboodle.admin/src/httpClient/authErrorInterceptor.ts` | 401: single-flight refresh via `update()`, one replay, else forced logout; auth endpoints excluded |
| `caboodle.admin/src/services/auth.service.ts` | `login`, `refreshAccessToken`, `logout` HTTP calls |
| `caboodle.admin/src/services/authClient.service.ts` | In-memory token cache, `triggerRefresh`, `clearAll` |
| `caboodle.admin/src/services/authSession.service.ts` | Central `logout(reason)`, toast on expiry, `?redirect=` builder, `consumePostLoginRedirect`, `isSafeRelativePath` |
| `caboodle.admin/src/services/authBroadcast.service.ts` | `BroadcastChannel("cbdl_admin_auth")` with `storage`-event fallback; messages `LOGIN`, `LOGOUT`, `TOKEN_REFRESHED` |
| `caboodle.admin/src/services/storage.service.ts`, `auth.constants.ts` | Storage adapters; `LOGIN_ROUTE`, `caboodle:postLoginRedirect`, legacy keys cleared on logout |
| `caboodle.admin/src/hooks/useAuth.ts` | `login`, `logout` (revoke first), `getToken` |

- **Data:** NextAuth JWT cookie (access token, refresh token, expiries, names, image); sessionStorage `caboodle:postLoginRedirect`.
- **APIs/interfaces:**

| Method | Path | Access rule | Request / Response | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | /api/v1/admin/login | `AllowAnonymous` | `TokenRequest(Email, Password)` / `AuthDto` | `AdminController.LoginAsync` → `TokenService.GetAdminTokenAsync` |
| GET, POST | /api/auth/[...nextauth] (admin Next.js route) | NextAuth | session, credentials callback, `update()` | `caboodle.admin/src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts` |

  Also uses `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh-token` and `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` (2.1.1).
- **Business rules:** admin check runs after the password check, so a wrong password never reveals admin status; the redirect target must be a same-origin relative path (rejects `//`, `/\`, schemes); logout is idempotent for 1.5 s; a broadcast logout does not re-broadcast.
- **Dependencies:** next-auth; env `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` (present in all four admin env files), `NEXT_PUBLIC_NEXTAUTH_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_CABOODLE_API_URL`.
- **Errors & edge cases:** a 401 on `refresh-token` forces logout with reason `expired`; server-side axios 401s are not refreshed (left to the page guard); `setTimeout` is clamped to 24 days.
- **Tests:** backend `TokenServiceTests.GetAdminTokenAsyncChecksPasswordBeforeAdminRole`. `caboodle.admin` has no test files at all.
- **Gotchas / tech debt:** refresh uses the shared `POST /auth/refresh-token`, which does not re-check the ADMIN role, so an account whose ADMIN role is removed keeps a refreshable admin session (permission checks still fail after the 10-minute permission cache). The admin JWT shares the signing key and claims with app tokens, so an app token is accepted by admin endpoints when the user holds the permissions (no audience separation).

### 2.2 Module: Organizations & Access Control

- **Purpose:** Owns the IAM model introduced by CS-1770: companies (organizations of type Brand or Brokerage), people's memberships and roles in them, brokerage to brand connections, per-member brand and module access, the module catalog and its per-organization assignments, per-organization module settings and limits, the IAM audit trail, and the access engine that every other module's endpoints use to decide who may do what. It replaces the legacy user-role model (`BRANDOWNER`, `BROKER`, `BRANDSUBUSER`, `BROKERSUBUSER` in `caboodle.backend/caboodle/src/BuildingBlocks/Core/Shared/Authorization/CaboodleRoles.cs`) as the source of authorization for the customer app.
